explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/520: for a Rademacher multiplicative f (f(p) i.i.d. uniform ±1 over primes, f multiplicative on squarefree n, 0 on non-squarefree n), is there c > 0 with limsup Σ_{m≤N} f(m)/√(N log log N) = c almost surely? IsRademacherMultiplicative encodes: measurable, independent, uniform ±1 values at primes; f(1) = 1; multiplicativity on coprime pairs; f = 0 off squarefree numbers (so f(0) = 0). Together these determine f(n) = ∏ f(p) on squarefree n, matching the page. The theorem negates the existence of c > 0 such that, on every probability space and for every such f, the limsup equals c a.s.; since the law is the same on every space, this is equivalent to the page's question answered negatively. The page itself records only Harper's conjecture that the answer is no (Σ ≪ √N (log log N)^{1/4+o(1)}), while the docstring cites Høystad [Hø26] and a linked formal proof establishing that bound, which makes the true limsup 0 (a genuine value, not a junk one), so the negation is the intended content. Finitely many small N where log log N ≤ 0 are irrelevant to the limsup. Faithful.
